extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy (metaphysics, philosophy of mind)
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic exposition of the fundamental data of philosophy: distinguishing orders of mental manifestations (vivid vs faint), the grounds for the subject/object distinction, and the philosophical genesis and status of space, time, matter, motion, and force. Intended as a conceptual framework for thinking about perception, reality, and the forms of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into vivid and faint manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: All manifestations of the Unknowable are divisible into two classes — vivid manifestations and faint manifestations; the differential characteristic between these orders must be specified because the conditions under which each order occurs are different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that vivid and faint manifestations have distinct conditions of occurrence and behavior; the classification is foundational for subsequent philosophical claims about subject and object. Examples include colours and visible forms (vivid) versus ideas/memories (faint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals versus copies (vivid vs faint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those of the one order (vivid) are originals, while those of the other order (faint) are copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrast highlights ontological status: vivid manifestations present as primary occurrences, faint ones as reproductions or derivations (e.g., memories, ideas). Use this distinction when attributing primacy or dependency among mental phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series continuity of each current
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid manifestations form a series or heterogeneous current that is never broken; faint manifestations likewise form a parallel series or current that is never broken (no direct knowledge of breakage of either).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the continuous, stream-like nature of both orders; treat each as possessing an ongoing continuity that structures experience and thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion properties (longitudinal and transverse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those of the first order (vivid) cohere with one another not only longitudinally but also transversely, and these cohesions are indissoluble; those of the second order (faint) also cohere longitudinally and transversely but their cohesions are mostly dissoluble with ease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cohesion (how tightly manifestations bind together across time and among themselves) as a diagnostic: indissoluble cohesion marks vivid phenomena; dissoluble cohesion marks faint phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-current independence (vivid unmodifiable by faint)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two currents (vivid and faint) running side by side have little coherence — the great body of the vivid current is absolutely unmodifiable by the faint, and the faint may become almost separate from the vivid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates asymmetry in interaction: do not assume faint ideas can readily alter vivid manifestations; consider how certain vivid events intrude regardless of faint trains of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of occurrence belong to same order
rubrics_metrics.description: The conditions under which manifestations of either order occur themselves belong to that order: for the faint order, the conditions are always present among the faint manifestations; for the vivid order, the conditions are often not present and lie outside the current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing causation or producibility, look within the same order for the relevant conditions for faint phenomena, but do not expect antecedent conditions to be present among the vivid manifestations in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traceability and controllability of antecedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Manifestations of the faint order have traceable antecedents; can be made to occur by establishing their conditions and can be suppressed by establishing other conditions. Manifestations of the vivid order often occur without previous presentation of antecedents and may persist or cease under known or unknown conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use traceability as a criterion: if an experience has clear antecedents and is controllable by conditions, treat it as faint; if it arises unexpectedly without antecedents (e.g., flash of lightning, sudden sounds, a wound from a blow), treat it as vivid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotions and muscular tensions are special vivid manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotions and sensations of muscular tension are vivid manifestations which, although they can be produced by faint manifestations (ideas), are habitually classed apart from other vivid manifestations like colours, sounds, pressures, smells, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize exceptions: emotions and bodily tensions straddle the orders — produced by ideas yet ontologically treated apart; account for these special cases when applying the vivid/faint distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence among faint manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many manifestations of the faint order are partly caused by vivid manifestations (memories, suggestions), but these results mainly depend on antecedents belonging to the faint order — each faint manifestation depends on its relations to other faint manifestations that have gone before or coexist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In explaining faint phenomena (thought trains, inferences), emphasize internal relations among faint states (prior thoughts, coexisting ideas) as the main determinants; external vivid triggers may modulate but are not usually primary causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primordial division corresponds to subject and object (ego/non-ego)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental division between the two orders corresponds to the distinction between object and subject: faint manifestations (a continuous whole differing in quantity, quality, cohesion, and conditions) are called the ego; vivid manifestations, indissolubly bound in large masses and with independent conditions, are called the non-ego.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming the subject/object dichotomy, base the attribution on the seven salient characters of the two orders (vivid/faint), and interpret 'ego' and 'non-ego' as the powers manifesting respectively in faint and vivid forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reality as persistence in consciousness (test of reality)
rubrics_metrics.description: By reality is meant persistence in consciousness — a persistence that is either unconditional (e.g., consciousness of space) or conditional (e.g., consciousness of a body while grasping it). Persistence is the ultimate test by which we separate the real from the unreal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply persistence as the practical criterion of reality: if an impression or presence resists being expelled from consciousness under expected conditions, predicate reality. This yields distinctions among absolute and relative reality and justifies treating persistent effects as equivalents of their persistent causes for practical purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought is in relations; Time and Space as abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought always consists of relations. Relations are of two orders — relations of sequence and relations of co-existence. The abstract of all sequences is Time; the abstract of all co-existences is Space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relational account to ground definitions: view time as the abstraction from recurrent sequence relations and space as the abstraction from co-existence relations. Reject treating Time and Space as original intuitions beyond relational genesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genesis of Space from experiences of force and muscular adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Consciousness of Space is a consciousness of co-existent positions, originally ascertained by touch; each position is disclosed by the resistance of an object and the muscular tension we exert. Thus experiences of forces variously correlated are those from which our consciousness of Space is abstracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explaining spatial concepts, ground them in embodied experiences (touch, resistance, muscular adjustments). Do not postulate an absolute Space beyond these experiential origins; accept space as a relative abstraction useful for reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate use of relative realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative realities (the forms of our consciousness) are effects of absolute reality, but because they persist and stand in indissoluble relation with their unconditioned cause, we may legitimately continue to deal with them as equivalents of absolutes in practical reasoning — provided we understand them as relative, not absolute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reasoning and scientific practice, treat persistent relative entities (space, time, bodies) as real-operational equivalents of whatever unconditioned cause produces them, while retaining philosophical awareness of their relativity.
